passage:
A village built a community Wi-Fi network in the town square. Students could do homework online, farmers could check weather, and small shops could accept digital payments.
The network helped many people, but it also made the square busier. Some students stayed late playing games, and older residents complained about noise.
The village added rules: quiet hours, study tables, and a helper desk for people learning to use phones.
The Wi-Fi brought access, but access needed management.
A public resource becomes valuable when it is shared fairly. Internet connection may be invisible, but its effects appear in real places among real people.
